entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

Item D, on the page-4 skyline columns (the Column component in Skyline.tsx and its labels; re-read first). Atahan: "I want my decisions to be much more visible in Prioritize, and if the AI later proposes changing my decision because of new data, that must be visible on the column itself too."

   - the column's outline or edge drawn in sweep blue (keep the domain hue as the fill, so domain stays readable);

4. **Priorities list:** confirmed rows show "PM ✓" in blue, and challenged rows sort to the top with a white "!".
5. Add rows for these marks (PM-confirmed and challenged) to the page-4 Guide legend.

Address this before completing your current task.

+// The PM's position and challenges to it, shared by the skyline, the matrix and the list (page 4): a confirmed band is
+// the one blue mark ("M ✓"); an open proposal against it is white attention ("!", "AI: Should ▼ · cause").
+import type { Band, PrioritizePayload, Proposal, Target } from "@/lib/prioritize";
+export const BAND_RANK: Record<Band, number> = { Must: 0, Should: 1, Could: 2 };
+export interface Challenge { band: Band; from: Band; cause: string }
+/** Open proposal against the PM-confirmed band of this target, if any. */
+export function challengeOf(d: PrioritizePayload, t: Target): Proposal | null {
+  return openProposals(d).find((p) => p.against === "pm" && p.key === t.key && p.line === t.line && p.market === t.market) ?? null;
+export const arrow = (to: Band, from: Band | null) => (from && BAND_RANK[to] < BAND_RANK[from] ? "▲" : "▼");

Code: `src/bmw_req/prioritize/` (`__init__.py` schema, `score.py` stage `prioritize`, `gate.py` stage `gate`, `run.py` CLI),
`api/routers/prioritize.py`, tests `tests/test_prioritize.py`. Shared helpers factored out of score-v3 without changing it:
`scoring.voice_curve / shrink / renormalised / cap_unobserved / align_basic`, `fit.luna_then_sol`.

```
uv run python -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1                     gate, then prioritize
uv run python -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1 --stage prioritize  re-score only (free)
uv run python -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1 --stage gate --pilot 5 [--only rq:… …]   print, store nothing
uv run python -m bmw_req.prioritize.run --checkpoint cp1 --report            bands per market + top-5 with factors
```

- **Weights** live in `weights_version` as `{"scheme": "prio-v1", "weights": {…}}`; score-v3's `current_weights` skips rows
  with a `scheme`. `POST /api/prioritize/weights {weights, rationale, actor?}` (human audit `change_weights`) — used by the
  next prioritize run.
- **Customer voice:** area comments carry no severity, so each counts at score-v3's medium severity (share × 2/3 before
  the log curve). Comment base = in-scope extract-v4 comments visible at the checkpoint per line × market; < 30 → borrow.
- **Satisfaction gap:** study items = the requirement's `study:` ids ∪ its area themes' supporting / contradicting study
  edges, matched by item text to the line's derivatives × market.
- **Competitive gap:** numeric only when the rung has a numeric baseline AND a cited / projected threshold; otherwise the
  fallback (tier-weighted `competes_with` edges on the area's themes, sources in that market or global, /4). With no
  competitor evidence it counts 0 (not renormalised, as score-v3's competitive pressure). `factors[].method` =
  `numeric | fallback | none`; explanations start with "fallback (…)"; flags `competitive_fallback` / `competitive_none`.
- **Portfolio leverage:** spread = min(0.5, (targets − 1) / 6) + enabler credit (two passes: base without credit → credit).
- **Future relevance:** trends = requirement `trend_ids` ∪ theme `trend_for` edges in that market (0.1 each, ≤ 0.3); Kano
  drift 0.2 for performance / delighter requirements with competitor or trend evidence.
- **Confidence level:** E1 ≥ 20 own comments and (study or basis ≥ .7); E2 ≥ 10 comments, or ≥ 3 with study / basis ≥ .6,
  or study with basis ≥ .7; E3 ≥ 3 comments, study, basis ≥ .5 or define's `own_evidence`; else E4. Basis score =
  ½ chosen-rung basis + ½ mean over the rung's levels.
- **Effort:** keep_strength / package_variant S, change_design / add_feature / market_variant M, raise_capability L; +1 step
  when the aspects draw on ≥ 3 resources; then the rung shift.
- **Order of rules:** score → D-038 no-comment cap (own evidence = satisfaction gap AND competitive gap ≥ .5) → D-038 one
  band for Kano-basic needs → bundle band → choose-jointly flags → rationale. Rank within line × market = score order (a bundle-lifted band does not move a member up the ranking).
- **Flags** (page 4 parses `kind|arg|arg`): `brand_blocked` (brand fail, D-008), `brand_fail|warn`-style `brand_warn`,
  `segment_warn` / `segment_fail`, `gate_pending`, `borrowed_voice` (no comment base of its own, D-038), `no_comment_cap`,
  `basic_aligned`, `bundle_band|<band>`, `volume_conflict` (BMW file vs public), `competitive_fallback` / `competitive_none`,
  `choose_jointly|<via>|<partner key>`.
- **Payload shapes (match `web/src/lib/prioritize.ts`):** `weights = {scheme, version, factors, bands: {Must, Should}}`;
  `markets` = list; unavailable factors have `value: null, points: 0, available: false`; proposals' `factor_delta` =
  points per factor (`explain`, `against`, `score`, `prev_score` alongside; status may also be `superseded`); target detail
  `history[] = {checkpoint, label, run_id, score, band, rank, rung, rationale, confirmed}`, `evidence = {comments, study,
  research, options, insights, own_market, count, by_kind, trend_ids, factors}`; what-if = `{key, line, market, level,
  score, band, base, delta, modifiers, confidence, effort, rationale, before, exposures: [{key, title, via, relation,
  strength, band, note}], exposure_summary: ["+1 exposure via mass"]}`.
- **Agent-panel events** (`audit_event`, actor `structure.gate` / `structure.prioritize`): gate `start {requirements,
  to_check, carried}` → one `check {key, checked, to_check, brand, segments, markets, by, error}` per finished requirement
  → `finished {stats}`; prioritize `scored {targets, by_band, bundles, proposals, flags}`.
- **Gate:** `prio_fit` holds one brand / segment / market / feasibility row per target (brand is per requirement, segment
  per line, both repeated per target); `checked_by` = `luna | sol | carried:<…>`. Static instructions + portfolio reference
  first (prompt cache), then one requirement; sol re-checks brand / segment / market warn / fail at reasoning effort low.
- **Proposals:** reference band = the latest PM decision visible at the checkpoint, else the parent run's band; every
  re-score supersedes the target's open proposals (status `open | accepted | rejected | superseded`). Accepting writes a
  `prio_decision` (audit `proposal_accepted` + `confirm_priority`); a direct decision supersedes open proposals.
- **Decision:** body adds optional `cp` and `override_brand`; a Must / Should on a brand-`fail` target needs
  `override_brand: true` (409 otherwise); actor falls back to `X-Actor`; rationale ≥ 5 chars.
- **Target** adds `version`, `own_band` (band before the bundle rule), `effort`, `gaps`, `confidence.{basis_score, comments,
  study}`, `factors[].{label, method}`; `gates` are objects `{result, rationale, checked_by}`. AI re-scores write
  `audit_event` rows (actor `structure.prioritize`, action `rescore`, entity `prio_target`, id `key|line|market`).

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("foundation/documents/prioritization.md"); s = p.read_text()
a = '''- **Weights** live in `weights_version` as `{"scheme": "prio-v1", "weights": {…}}`; score-v3's `current_weights` skips rows
  with a `scheme`. `POST /api/prioritize/weights {weights, rationale, actor?}` (human audit `change_weights`) — used by the
  next prioritize run.'''
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, '''- **Weights and bands** live in `weights_version` as `{"scheme": "prio-v1", "weights": {six factors}, "bands": {Must,
  Should}}` (rows without `bands` = 60 / 45); score-v3's `current_weights` and process.py's `_current_weights` skip rows with
  a `scheme`. `score.py` reads both from the current version (`current_config` / read-only `stored_config`; `band_for`
  replaces the hard-coded 60 / 45 in the prio-v1 path, `score_all(…, bands=)`). Validation: exactly the six factors, each
  ≥ 0, sum > 0; 0 < Should < Must ≤ 100. Versions are numbered WITHIN the scheme (v1 = the system default row;
  `weights_version.id` is shared with score-v3 and is returned as `id`).
  - `POST /api/prioritize/weights {factors, bands, rationale, actor?}` (legacy `weights` = `factors`; `bands` omitted =
    keep) → new version + human audit `change_weights` (old / new factors + bands, rationale) → automatic re-score of
    every checkpoint cp1 → cp2. Returns `{weights_version (scheme number), id, factors, bands, rescore}`.
  - `GET /api/prioritize/weights/history?limit=` → `{current, defaults, history: [{version, id, factors, bands, actor, at,
    rationale, default}]}`. Revert = load an earlier version and save it again (a new version).
  - `POST /api/prioritize/preview {factors, bands, cp, line?, market?}` → every target re-scored IN MEMORY through the same
    `score_all` path (no writes): `targets[] {key, line, market, score, band, prev_score, prev_band (stored latest run),
    confirmed}`, `summary {targets, by_band, changes, moves {"Must→Should": n}, decisions_affected}`, `changes[]`,
    `decisions_affected[]` (PM decisions whose band the new AI band would contradict → would get a proposal).
  - GET `/api/prioritize` `weights` adds `id, actor, at, rationale, default, defaults {factors, bands}` and a `rescore`
    status (`{state: idle | running, seq, done, last, error}`; also `GET /api/prioritize/rescore`).
  - Page 4: "Weights vN" pill in the HUD controls opens a panel on the far left under the HUD (where the matrix goes; one
    of the two at a time): grouped sliders Customer / Business (market weight "stylized (Q-015)") / Future with each
    factor's and group's share, Must / Should threshold sliders (the skyline planes follow), debounced (250 ms) preview →
    the skyline columns morph to the previewed scores / AI bands (PM bands stay), "n band changes", moves, "PM decisions
    → proposal"; Save needs a rationale; Reset; last 6 versions (click = load). HUD micro line: "Scoring formula prio-v1 ·
    weights vN (default, D-050 | by <actor>, <date>)".
- **Automatic re-score (`src/bmw_req/prioritize/auto.py`, worker `api/rescore.py`):** after `POST /decision` and
  `POST /proposal/{id}` (re-score the LATER checkpoints only: inputs at the decision's own checkpoint did not change),
  `POST /weights` (all checkpoints), `POST /api/definition/choice` (from the choice's checkpoint, or all) and
  `POST /api/definition/link-review` (all: link reviews apply everywhere). The POST commits, then queues and returns
  `rescore: "queued"` (`"none"` when nothing is later). One daemon worker thread on its own SQLite connection; requests
  during a run coalesce into one follow-up pass from the earliest requested checkpoint; ~0.1 s per checkpoint. Only
  checkpoints that already have a prioritize run are re-run; each is a normal new `checkpoint_run` (stats `trigger:
  "auto:<trigger>"`) and logs `audit_event` actor `structure.prioritize`, action `auto_rescore {trigger, from, runs}`.
  `PRIO_AUTO_RESCORE=thread | sync | off` (default `off` under pytest; tests set `sync`). The page polls
  `/api/prioritize/rescore` until idle, then refetches page 4 (all checkpoints); HUD shows "re-scoring…".
- **Cause `weights_changed`:** when the weights version differs from the previous run at the same checkpoint, the run also
  scores with the old weights; a proposal whose band only the weights moved gets cause `weights_changed` (after `pm_rung`).
- **Checkpoint visibility (fix):** a run supersedes only open proposals of ITS checkpoint; a decision supersedes open
  proposals at checkpoints where it is visible (its own and later); `GET /api/prioritize?cp=` lists proposals of the current
  run plus still-open ones from runs at visible checkpoints (cp1 never shows cp2's), one open proposal per target (newest);
  target detail filters proposals and decisions the same way; "previous score" rows come from visible checkpoints only.
- **Rejected proposals don't nag:** a proposal the PM rejected (after their latest decision on the target) is not re-proposed
  with the same old → new band until the score has moved ≥ 5 points.
- **Page 4 PM marks:** confirmed columns get a sweep-blue edge and a blue "M ✓" chip (base disc stays); a challenged
  decision (open proposal with `against: "pm"`) gets a white ring at the AI score and "! AI: Should ▼ · <cause>", pulsing
  once per checkpoint arrival; matrix cells ✓ / white "!" + proposed band; list rows "PM ✓" in blue, challenged first with
  "!". A compact HUD line "n of your decisions are challenged at JUL" lists them (requirement · line · market · your band →
  proposed · cause); a row opens the inspector. The inspector starts with "What you're deciding on" (statement, area,
  metric, the rung in use here with value and basis, ≤ 3 acceptance criteria, "View definition →"), shows bundle members as
  rows (target value, own score / band, "lifted to <band> by the bundle") and states the decision's scope (one requirement
  × line × market; bundle members keep their own decisions).''')
a = "every\n  re-score supersedes the target's open proposals"
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, "every\n  re-score supersedes the target's open proposals at its checkpoint")
p.write_text(s)
EOF
grep -n "Must ≥ 60 · Should ≥ 45 · Could\*\*. Weights" foundation/documents/prioritization.md

+  - `POST /api/prioritize/preview {factors, bands, cp, line?, market?}` → every target re-scored IN MEMORY through the same
+    `score_all` path (no writes): `targets[] {key, line, market, score, band, prev_score, prev_band (stored latest run),
+    confirmed}`, `summary {targets, by_band, changes, moves {"Must→Should": n}, decisions_affected}`, `changes[]`,
+    `decisions_affected[]` (PM decisions whose band the new AI band would contradict → would get a proposal).
+  - GET `/api/prioritize` `weights` adds `id, actor, at, rationale, default, defaults {factors, bands}` and a `rescore`
+    status (`{state: idle | running, seq, done, last, error}`; also `GET /api/prioritize/rescore`).
+  - Page 4: "Weights vN" pill in the HUD controls opens a panel on the far left under the HUD (where the matrix goes; one
+    of the two at a time): grouped sliders Customer / Business (market weight "stylized (Q-015)") / Future with each
+    factor's and group's share, Must / Should threshold sliders (the skyline planes follow), debounced (250 ms) preview →
+    the skyline columns morph to the previewed scores / AI bands (PM bands stay), "n band changes", moves, "PM decisions
+    → proposal"; Save needs a rationale; Reset; last 6 versions (click = load). HUD micro line: "Scoring formula prio-v1 ·
+  `POST /proposal/{id}` (re-score the LATER checkpoints only: inputs at the decision's own checkpoint did not change),
+  `POST /weights` (all checkpoints), `POST /api/definition/choice` (from the choice's checkpoint, or all) and
+  `POST /api/definition/link-review` (all: link reviews apply everywhere). The POST commits, then queues and returns
+  `rescore: "queued"` (`"none"` when nothing is later). One daemon worker thread on its own SQLite connection; requests
+  during a run coalesce into one follow-up pass from the earliest requested checkpoint; ~0.1 s per checkpoint. Only
+  checkpoints that already have a prioritize run are re-run; each is a normal new `checkpoint_run` (stats `trigger:
+  "auto:<trigger>"`) and logs `audit_event` actor `structure.prioritize`, action `auto_rescore {trigger, from, runs}`.
+  `PRIO_AUTO_RESCORE=thread | sync | off` (default `off` under pytest; tests set `sync`). The page polls
+  `/api/prioritize/rescore` until idle, then refetches page 4 (all checkpoints); HUD shows "re-scoring…".
+- **Cause `weights_changed`:** when the weights version differs from the previous run at the same checkpoint, the run also
+  scores with the old weights; a proposal whose band only the weights moved gets cause `weights_changed` (after `pm_rung`).
+- **Checkpoint visibility (fix):** a run supersedes only open proposals of ITS checkpoint; a decision supersedes open
+  proposals at checkpoints where it is visible (its own and later); `GET /api/prioritize?cp=` lists proposals of the current
+  run plus still-open ones from runs at visible checkpoints (cp1 never shows cp2's), one open proposal per target (newest);
+  target detail filters proposals and decisions the same way; "previous score" rows come from visible checkpoints only.
+- **Rejected proposals don't nag:** a proposal the PM rejected (after their latest decision on the target) is not re-proposed
+  with the same old → new band until the score has moved ≥ 5 points.
+- **Page 4 PM marks:** confirmed columns get a sweep-blue edge and a blue "M ✓" chip (base disc stays); a challenged
+  decision (open proposal with `against: "pm"`) gets a white ring at the AI score and "! AI: Should ▼ · <cause>", pulsing
+  once per checkpoint arrival; matrix cells ✓ / white "!" + proposed band; list rows "PM ✓" in blue, challenged first with
+  "!". A compact HUD line "n of your decisions are challenged at JUL" lists them (requirement · line · market · your band →
+  proposed · cause); a row opens the inspector. The inspector starts with "What you're deciding on" (statement, area,
+  metric, the rung in use here with value and basis, ≤ 3 acceptance criteria, "View definition →"), shows bundle members as
+  rows (target value, own score / band, "lifted to <band> by the bundle") and states the decision's scope (one requirement
+  × line × market; bundle members keep their own decisions).
- **Customer voice:** area comments carry no severity, so each counts at score-v3's medium severity (share × 2/3 before
the log curve). Comment base = in-scope extract-v4 comments visible at the checkpoint per line × market; < 30 → borrow.
- **Satisfaction gap:** study items = the requirement's `study:` ids ∪ its area themes' supporting / contradicting study
per line, both repeated per target); `checked_by` = `luna | sol | carried:<…>`. Static instructions + portfolio reference
first (prompt cache), then one requirement; sol re-checks brand / segment / market warn / fail at reasoning effort low.
- **Proposals:** reference band = the latest PM decision visible at the checkpoint, else the parent run's band; every
-  re-score supersedes the target's open proposals (status `open | accepted | rejected | superseded`). Accepting writes a
+  re-score supersedes the target's open proposals at its checkpoint (status `open | accepted | rejected | superseded`). Accepting writes a
`prio_decision` (audit `proposal_accepted` + `confirm_priority`); a direct decision supersedes open proposals.
- **Decision:** body adds optional `cp` and `override_brand`; a Must / Should on a brand-`fail` target needs
`override_brand: true` (409 otherwise); actor falls back to `X-Actor`; rationale ≥ 5 chars.

## Summary
All requested items are built: 1 (weights panel and bands), 2 (automatic re-score), plus the coordinator's A (checkpoint leak), B (challenged-decisions notice), C (what you're deciding on), D (PM marks on columns, matrix, list and guide) and the weights-panel feedback (far-left panel, per-scheme version numbers, plain wording, tooltip).

Checks:
- `uv run pytest -q`: 122 passed, 2 skipped, 3 failed. The 3 failures are the same legacy ones in tests/test_api.py.
- tests/test_prioritize.py: 14 passed, 5 of them new.
- `npx tsc -b --noEmit`: clean. `npm run build`: passes.
- Nothing was committed, and STATE.md / DECISIONS.md were not touched.

## Backend
**src/bmw_req/prioritize/score.py** (untracked file):
- **Weights and bands:** factor weights and Must/Should thresholds now come from the current prio-v1 weights version (`current_config` / read-only `stored_config`, `band_for`, `validate`). Validation rejects negative factors, all-zero factors, and anything outside 0 < Should < Must ≤ 100.
- **Versions:** numbered within the prio-v1 scheme (v1 = the default row). The shared row id is returned separately as `id`. History comes from `weights_history`.
- **Same formula everywhere:** `score_all`, `requirement_rules` and `score_target` all take `bands=`. `preview()` re-scores in memory through `score_all`, so the formula isn't duplicated.
- **`run(conn, cp, actor, trigger)`:** stores the trigger and bands in the run's stats. New cause `weights_changed`: when the weights changed since the last run at that checkpoint, the run also scores with the old weights, and a band that moved only because of the weights gets this cause (checked after `pm_rung`).
- **Rejected proposals don't come back:** if the PM rejected a proposal after their latest decision, the same old → new band is not proposed again until the score moves 5 points or more.
- **Checkpoint fix:** "previous score" rows now come only from checkpoints visible at that run's checkpoint.
- Legacy score-v3 is unchanged: scoring.py and process.py `_current_weights` still skip rows that have a `scheme` key.

**New files:**
- `src/bmw_req/prioritize/auto.py`: `rescore(conn, cp, trigger, include_self)`. Re-runs prioritize at that checkpoint and every later one, in order. It skips checkpoints that have never had a prioritize run and logs an `auto_rescore` audit event (actor `structure.prioritize`).
- `api/rescore.py`: the background worker.

**api/routers/prioritize.py:**
- **New endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/prioritize/preview {factors, bands, cp, line?, market?}`, which writes nothing.
  - `GET /api/prioritize/weights/history`.
  - `GET /api/prioritize/rescore`.
- **`POST /weights`** now takes `{factors, bands, rationale, actor?}` (`weights` still works as the old name). It returns the per-scheme version number and `rescore`.
- **GET `/api/prioritize`:** `weights` now also carries id, actor, at, rationale, default and defaults, and the payload has a `rescore` status.
- **`/decision` and `/proposal/{id}`** queue a re-score of the later checkpoints and return `rescore`.
- **Leak fix (A):**
  - Proposals now show only from runs at checkpoints visible at the requested cp (current run plus still-open ones), with one open proposal per target. cp1 now returns 0 proposals; it previously leaked 38.
  - Target detail filters proposals and decisions the same way.
  - A decision now closes open proposals only at its own and later checkpoints.
  - A run now closes only its own checkpoint's open proposals. Before, a cp2 run silently closed cp1's proposals.

**api/routers/definition.py:** one additive change. A `_rescore()` helper is called after the commit in `/choice` (from the choice's checkpoint) and `/link-review` (all checkpoints), and both return `rescore`.

## How auto re-score works
- The POST commits first, then calls `rescore.queue()` and returns `"queued"` immediately (or `"none"` when there is no later checkpoint).
- A single daemon thread on its own SQLite connection does the work.
- Requests that arrive while it runs are merged into one follow-up pass, starting from the earliest checkpoint any of them needs.
- One prioritize run takes about 0.07 s, and preview load plus scoring about 0.3 s.
- `PRIO_AUTO_RESCORE` = `thread` / `sync` / `off`. It defaults to `off` under pytest; the new tests set `sync`.
- The frontend (`rescore.ts`) polls `/api/prioritize/rescore` every 400 ms until idle, then refetches page 4 for all checkpoints. The HUD shows "re-scoring…" meanwhile.

## Frontend
**New files:** `weights.tsx`, `weights.css`, `rescore.ts`, `challenged.tsx`, `deciding.tsx`, `pm.ts`, `pm.css` (all under `web/src/screens/prioritize/`).

**Weights panel:** opens at the far left under the HUD, using `--phud-bottom` like the matrix. Only one of matrix and weights is open at a time.

**Edits to shared files** (each re-read right before editing, additive only):
- **PrioritizeHud.tsx:**
  - Weights pill in `.pcontrols` with the requested tooltip.
  - `<Challenged>` line right after `.pstats`, inside `.phud`.
  - HUD note now reads "Scoring formula prio-v1 · weights vN (default, D-050 / by actor, date)" plus "re-scoring…".
  - Weights panel rendering, and it closes when the matrix opens.
  - Inspector: `<Deciding>` above the score, `<BundleMembers>` rows, and a scope sentence on the decision box.
  - Matrix cells: ✓ for PM-confirmed, white "!" plus the proposed band for challenged.
  - Ranked list: "PM ✓" in blue, challenged rows first within each band, with "!".
- **Skyline.tsx:**
  - Preview scores and bands feed the column heights; the threshold planes follow the previewed bands.
  - PM-confirmed columns get a sweep-blue edge and a blue "M ✓" chip on the label.
  - Challenged columns get a white ring at the AI score and "! AI: Should ▼ · cause", pulsing once per arrival. Their labels win collisions.
  - The coordinator's bundle-dimming change is intact. No camera or transition code was touched.
- **data.ts:** `trackRescore` call in the decision and proposal onSuccess, and the `weights_changed` cause label.
- **definition/data.ts:** `trackRescore` in the choice and link-review onSuccess.
- **lib/prioritize.ts:** optional fields only (`weights_changed`, `rescore`, weights metadata, `Proposal.against`, `own_band`, `rung.by`).
- **guide.tsx:** legend rows for "Blue edge + M ✓" and "White ! + ring" on the skyline page, and the matrix rows.
- **topPanel.ts:** I added "weights" and then removed it again, so it is net unchanged.

**Docs:** foundation/documents/prioritization.md "As built" now covers weights and bands, preview, history and version numbering, auto re-score, `weights_changed`, the visibility fix, the no-repeat rule after a rejection, and the page-4 PM marks.

## Browser check (no saves)
- At /prioritize?cp=cp1 I opened Weights and dragged the Must slider. The preview showed "146 band changes", the moves list and "0 PM decisions → proposal", and the skyline columns and the MUST plane moved.
- At cp2 the inspector showed "What you're deciding on" (statement, area, metric, "Target ≤ 0.20 s · assumption · AI recommends target", 3 criteria, View definition →) and the scope line.
- Screenshots:
  - Preview: /var/folders/5l/pm7x789j3p733_szc6dmdttw0000gn/T/claude-chrome-screenshots-tMakAM/screenshot-1791711587898-22.jpg
  - Inspector: /var/folders/5l/pm7x789j3p733_szc6dmdttw0000gn/T/claude-chrome-screenshots-tMakAM/screenshot-1791711837314-23.jpg
- I fixed one layout bug found in the browser: panel rows were overlapping (now `grid-auto-rows: max-content`).

## Gaps
- **PM marks not seen live:** the blue cap, the challenged marks, the challenged-decisions line and the bundle rows could only be checked through types and tests, because the live DB has no PM decisions and I didn't create real ones.
- **Overlap at the bottom:** like the matrix, the weights panel's lower edge overlaps the open Agent dock body (both stop 96px from the bottom).
- **Console errors:** about 490 "synchronously unmount a root" errors appeared at 11:39:19. That was during the window when another session's missing DocumentPage import broke Vite/HMR, so it looks unrelated to my changes, but I didn't prove it.
- **Missing upstream runs:** if define/specify hasn't run at a checkpoint, the auto re-score skips it and records why in the `auto_rescore` event.
- **API server:** I restarted it once (pid 68992); it now runs as pid 70060, so someone else restarted it afterwards. Exactly one server is running.
- **Not part of this task:** the Inspector's proposal block still has a hard-coded "AI proposal · JAN → JUL" label (existing code).
